fields.features_heading: What Staff Get From Each Intake
fields.features_subheading: Every answer below lands in a field of its own on submit, ready for the conflict check and the attorney's first read.
fields.feature_1:
Different questions for a crash or a bite

Ask what kind of accident it was before anything else. A car crash opens questions about the vehicles and the police report, and a dog bite asks for the owner's name and the address.
fields.feature_2:
Every named party run against the client list

The app compares the other driver, the property owner, and each insurer with the firm's client list. A match holds the intake for whoever clears conflicts before an attorney sees it.
fields.feature_3:
Both insurers, each in separate fields

Ask for the person's own insurer and policy number, then the other side's insurer and any claim number already opened. Staff read each one from its own field, not from a paragraph.
fields.feature_4:
Injuries listed by body area

Let the person tick each injured area, such as neck, lower back, or right wrist, and describe the pain in their own words. The list sits at the top of the record the attorney opens.
fields.feature_5:
A witness section that repeats

Each witness gets a separate row with a name and a phone number. No one has to squeeze three names into one box, and staff can call each witness from the intake record itself.
fields.feature_6:
Code the firm can read and change

Every screen of the intake and its database schema go to your GitHub repository on paid plans. A developer the firm hires can read each line and change it like any other codebase.

fields.usecase_heading: Car, Fall, Dog Bite, and Bicycle Cases
fields.tab_content_1:
Held for conflicts when the other driver is a client

Tobiah Renfrew tells Haverline Injury Law that Wendell Ashgrove rear-ended him at a red light. The app finds Wendell Ashgrove on the firm's client list and holds the intake. Conflicts coordinator Imelda Ostrander gets an email with both names before any attorney opens it.
fields.tab_content_2:
Four photos from aisle 7 and the store's report number

Marisol Quenneville falls on a wet floor in aisle 7 of Pellham Market. She uploads 4 photos of the spill from her phone and types the incident report number the store gave her, IR-20417. Attorney Desmond Achterberg opens the photos and the report number from her intake record, not from an email thread.
fields.tab_content_3:
Three providers, each in a row of its own

A neighbor's dog bites Corentin Malabey on the forearm. He lists 3 providers: Eastgate Urgent Care, plastic surgeon Dr. Leonie Farquhar, and Stillwater Physical Therapy, each with a first visit date and a phone number. Paralegal Ysolde Partridge gets an email with all 3 rows and starts the records requests from those rows.
fields.tab_content_4:
After the last answer, a signature at 9:42 p.m.

A turning van knocks Oyelaran Fitch off her bike, and she fills in the intake on her phone that night, one question per screen. On the last screen she signs a statement that her answers are true. Intake coordinator Bram Kettleworth gets an email showing the signature saved beside her answers, with the time: 9:42 p.m.

fields.howto_title: How to Create a Personal Injury Intake Form
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to a personal injury intake form that checks names for conflicts and gives staff one clean record per intake.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 Decide which accidents the firm takes
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Write the conflict list as names
fields.howto_step_3_title: 03 Ask about the accident in order
fields.howto_step_1_des: List the case types your attorneys accept, such as car crashes and dog bites. Send every other choice to a short referral page. That first answer decides which set of questions opens next. Nobody fills in sections that do not apply to them.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Pull current and past clients, plus the companies and insurers the firm has dealt with, into one file of names. The app checks each named party against it. Spell the names the way staff already type them in the case file.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Put the date and the place first, then what happened. Ask about the vehicles or the property next, and any police or store report number. Give each fact its own field, and save one open box for the person's account in their own words.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Let the person tick injured body areas, then add one row per doctor or clinic with the date of the first visit and the office phone. Ask for names and dates only; the records themselves come later through the firm's own requests.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Ask for the person's own policy and the other side's insurer, with any claim number already opened. An upload for a photo of the insurance card brings in the policy number without anyone typing it.
fields.howto_step_6_title: 06 Choose who hears about each intake
fields.howto_step_6_des: Decide which intakes reach whom: a name match goes to the person who clears conflicts, a provider list to the paralegal, and everything else to the intake queue. Pick email, Slack, or an in-app alert for each one.
fields.howto_step_7_des: Send one that matches a current client, one with photos, and one from a phone. Check that each lands in its own record and that the right person hears about it, then change anything that is off by describing the fix in a prompt.

faq_plan.q: What is a personal injury intake form?
faq_plan.a: A personal injury intake form is a paper or digital document that gathers a prospective client's contact details and an account of the accident and resulting injuries. A lawyer uses the answers to check for conflicts and evaluate the case. In CasePeer's outline of intake, a fee agreement follows once the firm accepts the case and the client wants to move forward.

faq_plan.q: How do I create a personal injury intake form?
faq_plan.a: Describe it to Emergent's AI form builder in plain English. Name the accident types the firm takes and the client list to check names against, then say who hears about each intake. Emergent builds the form and the database behind it, and you change any part later by prompting.

faq_plan.q: What should an accident intake form ask about the accident itself?
faq_plan.a: Start with when and where it happened, then the person's own account. Then ask what fits the type: the vehicles and the road conditions for a crash, or the store's name and its incident report number for a fall. A separate field for each fact lets staff sort and search later.

faq_plan.q: Can a personal injury intake form list every provider a client has seen?
faq_plan.a: Yes. Make the provider section repeat: a person treated at urgent care, then by a surgeon, then at physical therapy adds one entry for each. The clinic's own pt intake form holds the clinical history. The firm's form only needs to show staff where treatment happened and whom to call.

faq_plan.q: How does a personal injury intake form help with a conflict check?
faq_plan.a: It hands whoever clears conflicts clean names instead of a paragraph. Ask for every other name each party uses, such as a former last name or a business name, and check each one. Emergent builds that check into the form from one line in your prompt, and a match waits for review before it reaches an attorney.

faq_plan.q: What insurance details belong on a personal injury intake form?
faq_plan.a: Ask for both sides. CasePeer's intake guide says the form should request insurance information for the client and the defendant, including the provider name, the policy number, and policy limits if available. Add any claim number the person already has, and let them skip a field they do not know.

faq_plan.q: How much medical detail should a personal injury intake form ask for?
faq_plan.a: Ask for enough to know what was hurt and who treated it: the injured body areas, a short description of the pain, and the providers seen. Leave diagnoses and session notes with the providers, much as a counselor's therapy intake form keeps that detail in the counselor's own records. A shorter form is easier to finish in one sitting.

faq_plan.q: Can someone fill out a personal injury intake form on a phone?
faq_plan.a: Yes. Emergent can build it as a conversational form that shows one question per screen, which keeps each screen readable on a small display. Scene photos and a picture of an insurance card upload from the same phone, next to the answers they belong to.

faq_plan.q: Can a personal injury intake form collect a signature?
faq_plan.a: Yes. An app built with Emergent can capture an e-signature on the last screen, for example under a statement that the answers are true, and save it beside the intake. Whether a signature meets any legal requirement is a question for the firm's own attorneys; the form only captures it.

faq_plan.q: Can a personal injury intake form record missed work and help at home?
faq_plan.a: Yes. Add fields for the employer, the workdays missed since the accident, and any paid help at home, such as an aide. When a care agency is involved, ask only for its name and start date; the agency's home care intake form holds the care plan. Every answer lands in a database the firm owns, with no response caps.

plan.angle: Eight of the top 10 are law firms' own PDF questionnaires and one is a template gallery; each stops at blank lines for the accident, the injuries and the insurer. This page shows the intake a personal injury firm runs once answers arrive: the other driver's name checked against the firm's client list before an attorney reads it, scene photos and a store report number kept in the record, every treating provider in a row of its own for staff to call, and a cyclist answering on her phone and signing a statement that her answers are true. The FAQ covers the definition, building one, what an accident intake form asks, provider lists, the conflict check, insurance fields, medical detail, phone completion, signatures, and missed work and help at home. No legal advice anywhere: the page describes what a firm collects and screens, never what a claim is worth or whether it is valid.
